summary: Captures requirements for a service that would let people browse and search the IETF's mailing list archives using ordinary IMAP email clients. It is a requirements memo meant as input to a later design and development effort, not a protocol specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo lists requirements for accessing IETF email archives through ordinary IMAP clients. It describes browsing, searching, access control, and user-specific read marks.

subtitle: Requirements for browsing and searching IETF mailing-list archives with IMAP clients.

tldr.problem: IETF participants wanted to browse and search mailing-list archives using standard IMAP clients.
tldr.mechanism: The memo lists requirements for exposing each list as a mailbox, supporting search and per-user read marks, and protecting the underlying archive from modification.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7017 is a requirements memo intended to inform later design and development, not a protocol specification.

today: RFC 7017 is an Informational requirements memo for IMAP access to IETF mailing-list archives. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement.

sections.title: Why IMAP Archive Access Is Wanted
sections.content:
The IETF uses email lists for its work and participants often need to access archived messages. RFC 7017 captures requirements for browsing and searching those archives with standard IMAP clients.

The memo is intended as input to a later activity for designing and developing the service. It does not specify that service's protocol or implementation.
sections.plainLanguage: People want to search old mailing-list messages in their usual email program. This memo describes what an archive service would need to do.

sections.title: Mailbox Access, Search, and Permissions
sections.content:
The archive should expose each list as an IMAP mailbox and work with standard IMAP clients. Users with credentials should have their own read/unread marks, while the interface must not let them insert, delete, or move archived messages.

Server-side search must be available and support multiple extensive searches. Restricted archives need credential-based access, while open archives must allow access with or without credentials.
sections.plainLanguage: Each mailing list appears as a mailbox that people can search. Users can mark messages as read, but cannot change the archived messages themselves.

sections.title: Authentication and Resource Use
sections.content:
When credentials are required, the service must use the datatracker's authentication system. Open archives should support anonymous access through SASL ANONYMOUS or an administrator-selected special username.

The RFC warns that extensive searches, many connections, copying messages, or large numbers of annotations can consume resources. Implementers should consider rate limits, quotas, and alerts for exceptional storage use.
sections.plainLanguage: Restricted lists require credentials, but open lists can be read anonymously. Searches and stored annotations need limits so they do not use too many resources.
